title: 'Objectivity simpliciter' (Def. 5) is self-referential / possibly empty; no cross-framework standard

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
Constraint (c) demands the account *secure* objectivity. But 'objectivity simpliciter' is defined as objective relative to some Φ 'whose postulates are not themselves rationally indicted *within* Φ' — Φ's own postulates vet Φ's own postulates. No criterion is given for choosing among admissible frameworks that is not itself framework-relative, so 'objectivity simpliciter' risks collapsing into 'objective relative to whichever Φ one adopted' — precisely the relativism the deflationist endorses. Def. 4/Def. 5 gesture at 'non-parochial criticism of postulates' but never define an agent-invariant, *cross-framework* standard.

Fix options: (a) define a genuine cross-framework agent-invariant standard for framework adoption; or (b) explicitly *scope* the adequacy thesis as conditional and prove the airtight weaker claim that conditional, framework-relative agent-invariant warrant ALREADY refutes deflationism (since ⊢_Φ Π is true-or-false independently of who endorses Φ — promote Lemma 5/R1), honestly declaring the cross-framework question out of scope with consequences spelled out.
